desc: Ideation: initial same-side/cross-side analysis; identified that cross-component moves merge components, so game length is not the naive fixed sum.
Deep analysis: terminal state is a single complete bipartite graph K_{x,N-x}; total moves = x*(N-x) - M.
Worker implemented DSU + formula Σ C(n_i,2) − M; passes all three samples but fails N=2,M=0.
Re-derived candidate rule: Aoki wins iff x*(N-x) - M is odd with x = Σ color-0 sides; passes all 3 samples plus N=1/M=0, N=2/M=0, N=3/M=0 hand checks.
Brute-force verify the candidate rule against exact minimax on all small bipartite graphs (N ≤ 5 exhaustive, N = 6 sampled): 0 mismatches across all tested graphs.
Finalize and write the complete Python solution (BFS 2-coloring, parity of x*(N-x) - M), O(N+M), reading stdin and printing Aoki/Takahashi.
